2026-11-01.title: Qudos Eetho Sunday · Sanctification of the Church
readings: The glory of the Lord and the Temple
Christ the cornerstone; a dwelling place for God
On this rock I will build my Church
2026-11-01.alt: Beginning of the liturgical year; the season of Annunciation (Suboro) begins. Note: the lectionary prints “Ex 10:1–5”; the setting up of the Tabernacle in Exodus 40:1–5 appears to be intended. Please confirm with the printed lectionary.
2026-11-01.verse: And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
theo: The Syro-Malankara year does not begin with Christmas or with Advent but with the Church. On Qudos Eetho Sunday we remember that God has sanctified a people for himself and made it his dwelling. Everything that follows in the year, the Annunciation, the Birth of the Lord, his Passion and Resurrection, is celebrated by this Church and for this Church.

The Old Testament readings trace the long story of God's dwelling. Moses sets up the Tabernacle; Solomon builds the Temple; Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord rise from the Temple and depart because of the people's sins; Isaiah sees the Lord enthroned, hears the seraphim cry “Holy, holy, holy” and is sent. God wants to live among his people, but his presence is holy, and it cannot be taken for granted.

The New Testament shows where that glory finally comes to rest. Christ himself is the cornerstone, and believers become “living stones… built into a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood” (1 Peter 2:5). In the Gospel, Peter confesses, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God”, and Jesus answers, “On this rock I will build my church.” The Church is not a human association; it is built by Christ, on the faith of Peter, and the powers of death will not overcome it.

For the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church this Gospel has a special meaning. In 1930 Archbishop Mar Ivanios and his companions, keeping the ancient West Syriac liturgy, entered full communion with the Bishop of Rome, the successor of Peter. Unity with Peter and fidelity to our own Antiochene heritage are not opposed; together they express the one Catholic Church built on the rock.
conn: The glory leaves and returns.

Ezekiel sees the glory depart from the Temple (10:18) and later return (43:4). John says of Christ: “the Word became flesh and lived among us” (John 1:14), literally “pitched his tent”. The glory has come back to dwell, in Christ and in his Church.
The song of the seraphim.
The “Holy, holy, holy” Isaiah heard in the Temple (6:3) is the hymn we sing at every Holy Qurbono before the anaphora. Each Sunday the parish joins the seraphim.
A royal priesthood.
1 Peter 2:9 applies to the baptised the words God spoke at Sinai: “You shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation” (Exodus 19:6).
The keys.
Peter receives the keys (Matthew 16:19) as Eliakim received “the key of the house of David” (Isaiah 22:22): a steward's authority, given for service.
altar: A church building is consecrated with holy Myron, and its altar becomes the place where heaven touches earth. But the walls are only a sign. At the Holy Qurbono the Church is built: “the Eucharist makes the Church” (Ecclesia de Eucharistia 26). Each time we receive the Body of Christ, we are made more truly the living stones of his house.
outline: Ask: why does our liturgical year begin with the Church, and not with Christmas?
Point 1 · God wants to dwell among us
From the Tabernacle to the Temple: God's desire is to live with his people. Show the glory departing in Ezekiel: holiness cannot be presumed.
1 Peter 2: each baptised person is a stone in God's house. Ask: what kind of stone am I, supporting or crumbling?
Peter's confession and Christ's promise. Speak of Mar Ivanios and the reunion of 1930: communion with Peter and fidelity to our Syriac heritage.
The seraphim's “Holy, holy, holy”, which we will sing in a few minutes: heaven's song in a parish church.
“I am a living stone in God's house this year.”
live: Be a living stone (1 Peter 2:5)
Choose one concrete way to support your parish this year: a ministry, a family unit, or helping someone come back to the Qurbono.
Pray “Holy, holy, holy” (Isaiah 6:3)
Each morning this week, pray the Trisagion slowly before starting work.
Pray for unity with Peter (Matthew 16:18)
Pray for the Pope and our Major Archbishop-Catholicos by name this week.
fathers: St Augustine

Preaching at the dedication of a church: “This is the house of our prayers, but we ourselves are the house of God.” What was done in building the walls is done in us when we are brought into faith and joined by love (Sermon 336).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He calls the Church the new Eden and the place where the Tree of Life, Christ, gives his fruit in the Mysteries (Hymns on Paradise).
magis: Lumen Gentium 6
The Church is called the building of God, the house in which his family dwells, the holy temple, built on Christ the cornerstone and on the foundation of the apostles.
Orientalium Ecclesiarum 2–3
The particular Churches of East and West are of equal dignity and are entrusted to the pastoral government of the Roman Pontiff, successor of Peter.
Catechism 756, 881
The Church as temple and living stones; Peter as the rock on which Christ built his Church.
saints: This week (as in the lectionary; confirm 2026–27 dates)
Commemoration of Bishop Paulose Mar Philexinos; the 318 Fathers of the Council of Nicaea; the 33 Martyrs of Melitene; All Holy Angels.
Servant of God Archbishop Mar Ivanios
Founder of the reunion movement (1930) and of the Bethany religious congregations; his cause for canonisation is in progress.
2026-11-01.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, cornerstone of your Church, sanctify us as living stones of your house. Keep us faithful to Peter's confession and to the faith of our fathers, that with the seraphim we may sing your holiness for ever. Amen.

2026-11-08.title: Hudos Eetho Sunday · Renewal of the Church
readings: My house shall be a house of prayer
Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the Temple
The Lord gathers and renews his people
To the lukewarm Church: I stand at the door and knock
Christ the high priest of the true sanctuary
Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up
2026-11-08.alt: Second Sunday of the liturgical year. (In the lectionary the Book of Revelation is read in the place of the Catholic Epistle.)
2026-11-08.verse: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
theo: Last Sunday we celebrated the Church as God's holy dwelling. Today, Hudos Eetho, we celebrate her renewal. The two belong together. The Church is holy because Christ sanctifies her, yet she is made of sinners and is always in need of purification. The Second Vatican Council says it plainly: the Church, “holding sinners in her bosom, is at the same time holy and always in need of being purified” (Lumen Gentium 8).

The readings show both the danger and the remedy. At the foot of Sinai the people make a golden calf, worshipping a god they can control. Solomon, dedicating the Temple, admits that “heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built” (1 Kings 8:27). God's house can never be our possession. The risen Christ says to the Church of Laodicea: “Because you are lukewarm… I am about to spit you out of my mouth” (Revelation 3:16). The danger of a Church is not only sin but comfort.

Jesus enters the Temple with a whip of cords and drives out the traders. His anger is not against worship but against worship turned into business. Then he points to himself: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” He was speaking of the temple of his body. The true renewal of the Church is always a return to Christ, crucified and risen, whose blood, says Hebrews, purifies “our conscience from dead works to worship the living God” (Hebrews 9:14).

Renewal does not come from outside the Church but from her own sources: the Word, the Mysteries, prayer and repentance. That is why the Lord, after rebuking Laodicea, says: “Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you.”
conn: The golden calf and the Lamb.
Israel melted gold to make a god they could see. In Christ, God gives himself visibly, not as gold but as the Lamb whose blood cleanses (Hebrews 9:12).
“A house of prayer for all peoples.”
Jesus quotes Isaiah 56:7 and Jeremiah 7:11. The traders filled the Court of the Gentiles, the one place where the nations could pray.
The Temple of his body.
John 2:21 is fulfilled at the Resurrection; the Church, his Body, becomes the temple where God is worshipped “in spirit and truth” (John 4:23).
Come to the waters.
Isaiah 55:1 invites the thirsty to buy “without money”; the free gift of grace flows from the side of Christ, the new Temple (Ezekiel 47:1; John 19:34).
altar: “I will come in to you and eat with you” (Revelation 3:20). At every Holy Qurbono the Lord who cleansed the Temple enters his Church and shares his table with us. Renewal begins at the altar, in a worthy and fervent communion, and spreads from there into the parish.
outline: Ask: if Jesus walked into our parish today, what would he praise, and what would he overturn?
Point 1 · Holy, yet always being purified
Lumen Gentium 8: the Church is holy and always in need of renewal. This is honesty, not shame.
Point 2 · The two dangers: idols and lukewarmness
The golden calf: a God we control. Laodicea: a Church that is comfortable. Name today's forms of both.
Point 3 · Renewal is a return to Christ
“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” Renewal comes from the risen Lord, through the Word, the Mysteries and repentance.
The Lord standing at the door and knocking: he wants to come in and eat with us.
“Lord, renew your Church, and begin with me.”
live: Remove one idol (Exodus 32)
Name one thing that takes God's place in your life, and set a limit to it this week.
Open the door (Revelation 3:20)
Make a good Confession this month, and prepare well for Holy Qurbono next Sunday.
Keep the house of prayer (Mark 11:17)
Arrive early for Qurbono and keep silence in church as a sign of reverence.
fathers: Origen
Commenting on John 2, he says the temple Jesus will raise is his body, and that the whole Church, as the body of Christ, will be raised and built as a living temple (Commentary on John 10).
St John Chrysostom
He warns that the Lord enters each soul as he entered the Temple, and asks whether we have made it a house of prayer or a market (Homilies on John 23).
magis: Lumen Gentium 8
The Church, embracing sinners in her bosom, is at the same time holy and always in need of purification, and follows constantly the path of penance and renewal.
Unitatis Redintegratio 6
Christ summons the Church to continual reformation, of which she always has need, insofar as she is a human institution.
Catechism 827
All members of the Church, including her ministers, must acknowledge that they are sinners; the Church therefore gathers sinners and is called to holiness.
saints: Consult the 2026–27 lectionary for the commemorations of this week. In the 2025–26 lectionary, St Theodore was remembered on this Sunday.
2026-11-08.prayer: Lord Jesus, you cleansed the Temple and raised up the temple of your body. Purify your Church, free us from idols and lukewarmness, and come in to eat with us at your holy table. Amen.

2026-11-15.title: Sunday of the Message to Zechariah
readings: A son for Abraham and Sarah
Do not fear, I am with you
The message to Zechariah in the Temple
2026-11-15.alt: First Sunday of the season of Annunciation (Suboro).
2026-11-15.verse: Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.
theo: The season of Suboro, the “good news”, opens not in Nazareth but in the Temple of Jerusalem, with an old priest burning incense. Zechariah and Elizabeth were “righteous before God”, yet they had no child, and they had grown old. God's first announcement in the New Testament is given to people who had prayed for years and seemed to have received no answer.

The Old Testament readings prepare us. Abraham and Sarah were given a son when it was humanly impossible; Abraham even laughed (Genesis 17:17). Hannah, barren and mocked, poured out her soul before the Lord in the sanctuary (1 Samuel 1:15) and became the mother of Samuel. Isaiah hears God say: “Do not fear, for I am with you.” The God of Israel brings life out of barrenness.

Zechariah's question is very human: “How will I know that this is so? For I am an old man.” He asks for a sign, and he receives one: silence until the promise is fulfilled. St Paul shows the opposite attitude in Abraham, who “hoping against hope… believed” and “grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God” (Romans 4:18, 20). Faith is not certainty that we can see; it is trust that God can do what he has promised.

John's mission is to go before the Lord “with the spirit and power of Elijah… to make ready a people prepared for the Lord” (Luke 1:17). Suboro is that preparation for us: a season in which the Church, like Zechariah in the Holy Place, waits, prays and lets God speak.
conn: Barren mothers, great sons.
Sarah (Isaac), Hannah (Samuel), the wife of Manoah (Samson) and Elizabeth (John): each birth shows that the future of God's people is God's gift, not human achievement.
The hour of incense.
Zechariah receives the message while the people pray outside at the hour of incense. In our Qurbono the incense rises with the prayers of the Church (Psalm 141:2; Revelation 8:3–4).
Elijah returns.
Malachi had promised that Elijah would come “to turn the hearts of parents to their children” (Malachi 4:5–6). The angel applies these words to John (Luke 1:17).
Ruth's “Where you go, I will go”.
Ruth's loyalty, a foreigner who becomes an ancestor of David and of Christ (Matthew 1:5), shows the faithful love that prepares the way of the Lord.
altar: Zechariah entered the sanctuary to offer incense; in every Holy Qurbono the priest does the same, and the people pray outside the veil as they did in the Temple. But we have more than Zechariah: the One whose coming he was promised now comes to the altar in his Body and Blood.
outline: Ask: have you ever prayed for something for years and thought God was not listening?
“Your prayer has been heard.” God's timing is not ours. Abraham, Hannah, Elizabeth.
His doubt is answered with silence, which becomes a school of faith. At the end his tongue is freed to praise (Luke 1:64).
Abraham's faith in Romans 4: trusting God when the facts say no.
John prepares hearts; Suboro prepares ours. Practical: reconciliation in families (“the hearts of parents to their children”).
“God has heard my prayer, even when I cannot see the answer.”
live: Keep praying (Luke 1:13)
Write down one intention you have prayed for a long time, and offer it again at this Sunday's Qurbono.
A week of holy silence (Luke 1:20)
Choose ten minutes of silence each day this week: no phone, no television, only God.
Turn hearts (Luke 1:17)
Take one step of reconciliation between parents and children in your family.
fathers: St Ambrose of Milan

Commenting on Luke, he praises Zechariah and Elizabeth as righteous in both the priestly and the married life, and sees in John's birth a sign that God's grace surpasses nature (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke, Book 1).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He contrasts the priest who doubted with the Virgin who believed: the one who questioned was silenced, while she who believed conceived the Word (Commentary on the Diatessaron).
magis: Catechism 523
St John the Baptist is the Lord's immediate precursor, sent to prepare his way; “prophet of the Most High”, he surpasses all the prophets.
Catechism 145–146
Abraham is the model of the obedience of faith; “hoping against hope”, he believed, and so became the father of all who believe.
Lumen Fidei 8–11
Abraham's faith is trust in a God who calls and promises, and who keeps his word even when it seems impossible.
saints: 16 Nov: St Matthew, Apostle (Malankara commemoration). 21 Nov: the Entrance of Mary, Mother of God, into the Temple. Confirm other commemorations in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-11-15.prayer: Lord God, you heard the prayer of Zechariah and Elizabeth and gave them a son to prepare the way of your Christ. Hear the prayers we have carried for so long, strengthen our faith when we cannot see, and make us a people prepared for the Lord. Amen.

2026-11-22.title: Sunday of the Annunciation to Mary, Mother of God
readings: The first promise: the woman and her offspring
Not by might, but by my Spirit
O that you would tear open the heavens and come down
We are called children of God
God sent his Son, born of a woman
The angel Gabriel is sent to Mary
2026-11-22.verse: Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.
theo: Last Sunday the angel came to an old priest in the Temple. Today the same angel, Gabriel, comes to a young virgin in Nazareth, a village never mentioned in the Old Testament. God's greatest work begins in a hidden house, in the heart of a woman who listens.

The readings stretch from the first pages of the Bible to its fulfilment. In the garden, after the first sin, God promises that the offspring of the woman will strike the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). Isaiah cries: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down” (Isaiah 64:1). St Paul answers: “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman” (Galatians 4:4). The Annunciation is the moment when heaven opens and God comes down.

“The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be holy; he will be called Son of God.” Mary conceives not by human power but by the Spirit, as Zechariah's vision promised: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit” (Zechariah 4:6). Her child is truly God and truly man; that is why the Church calls her Theotokos, Mother of God.

Zechariah asked, “How will I know?” and was silenced. Mary asks, “How can this be?” and then gives her free consent: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” The Fathers saw in her obedience the reversal of Eve's disobedience. Through her “yes”, the Son of God becomes our brother, and we become “children of God; and that is what we are” (1 John 3:1).
conn: Eve and Mary.
In Genesis 3 a woman listens to the serpent and humanity falls; in Luke 1 a woman listens to the angel and salvation enters the world. Genesis 3:15 is called the “first Gospel”.
The genealogy.
The evening Gospel (Matthew 1:1–17) lists sinners and saints, foreigners and kings. God's promise travels through a real, untidy family history to Mary, “of whom Jesus was born”.
The overshadowing.
The word Luke uses recalls the cloud that covered the Tabernacle (Exodus 40:35). Mary becomes the dwelling place of God.
Nothing is impossible.
“Nothing will be impossible with God” (Luke 1:37) echoes the Lord's words to Abraham about Sarah: “Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?” (Genesis 18:14).
altar: At the epiclesis of the Holy Qurbono the priest calls the Holy Spirit upon the bread and wine, as the Spirit came upon Mary. The same Lord who took flesh in her womb becomes present on the altar. Mary's “let it be with me” is the best preparation for Holy Communion.
outline: Contrast: an angel in the Temple to a priest (last week); an angel in a village house to a girl (today).
Genesis 3:15 to Galatians 4:4: God never forgot his first promise.
“Not by might, nor by power.” Christ comes by the Spirit's power, not by human means. Mary is truly Mother of God.
Point 3 · Mary's question and Mary's yes
Faith may ask questions; it ends in surrender. Compare Zechariah.
Where is God asking for my yes this week: a vocation, a forgiveness, a hidden duty?
“Here am I, Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
live: Pray the Angelus (Luke 1:38)
Pray the Angelus at noon every day this week; in the family, at least once together.
Say yes to one hidden duty
Do one task you have been avoiding at home or at work, quietly, as your “let it be”.
Honour the Mother of God
Pray one decade of the Rosary each evening, meditating on the Annunciation.
fathers: St Irenaeus of Lyons
“The knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary; what the virgin Eve bound through unbelief, the Virgin Mary set free through faith” (Against Heresies III, 22, 4).
St Bernard of Clairvaux
He imagines the whole world waiting for Mary's reply: Adam, Abraham, David and all the fathers beg her to answer the angel quickly and give her consent (Homilies in Praise of the Virgin Mother 4, 8).
magis: Lumen Gentium 56
Mary was not a merely passive instrument but cooperated in human salvation by free faith and obedience; the Fathers compare her with Eve: “death through Eve, life through Mary”.
Catechism 490–495
Mary, “full of grace”, was prepared by God; she is truly Mother of God (Theotokos) because she is the mother of the eternal Son made man.
Redemptoris Mater 13
At the Annunciation Mary entrusted herself to God completely, with the “obedience of faith”, responding with all her human and feminine “I”.
saints: 23 Nov: St Clement of Rome, Pope and Martyr. 25 Nov: St Catherine of Alexandria. 29 Nov: St Jacob of Serugh (Mar Jacob of Sarug), great Syriac poet (falls on Sunday in 2026). Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-11-22.prayer: Lord God, you sent your angel to the Virgin Mary, and by the power of the Holy Spirit your Son took flesh in her womb. Give us her listening heart and her generous “yes”, that Christ may be formed in us. Through her prayers, Mother of God, keep us faithful. Amen.

2026-11-29.title: Sunday of the Visitation of Mary, Mother of God, to Elizabeth
readings: The deaf shall hear, the blind shall see
God desires everyone to be saved
2026-11-29.alt: Third Sunday of Suboro. The Twenty-Five Days Nombu (fast before Yaldo) begins on Tuesday 1 December.
2026-11-29.verse: And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
theo: After the angel leaves, Mary does not stay at home to enjoy her secret. St Luke says she “set out and went with haste” to the hill country to visit Elizabeth. The first thing the Mother of God does, with the Son of God in her womb, is to serve. Faith that has received Christ goes out.

When Mary greets Elizabeth, the child John leaps in his mother's womb and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit. John, who will later point to the Lamb of God, recognises him already before birth. Elizabeth cries out: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb… why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” With these words the Church has greeted Mary ever since.

Mary answers with the Magnificat: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.” Her song is full of the Old Testament, especially Hannah's song: “My heart exults in the LORD… He raises up the poor from the dust” (1 Samuel 2:1, 8). God looks on the lowly, scatters the proud, fills the hungry, and remembers his mercy to Abraham. Mary sings not about herself but about God.

The readings also praise faithful women: Rebekah's kindness at the well (Genesis 24), the capable wife of Proverbs 31, whose strength is the fear of the Lord. Mary is blessed above all because she believed. And St Paul reminds us that God “desires everyone to be saved” (1 Timothy 2:4). The Visitation is the first Christian mission: Christ carried to a home, and a home filled with joy.
conn: The Ark comes to the hill country.

David asked, “How can the ark of the LORD come into my care?” and the ark stayed three months in the house of Obed-edom (2 Samuel 6:9–11). Elizabeth asks, “Why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” and Mary stays about three months (Luke 1:56). Mary is the new Ark.
Hannah and Mary.
Both sing after God has worked a wonder in a woman's womb; both praise the God who lifts up the lowly.
Rebekah at the well.
Rebekah's prompt, generous service to a stranger (Genesis 24:18–20) foreshadows Mary hurrying to serve Elizabeth.
The deaf hear, the blind see.
Isaiah 29:18 is fulfilled when the unborn John “hears” Mary's greeting and leaps for joy.
altar: Mary carried Christ hidden within her into Elizabeth's house. After every Holy Qurbono we too go home carrying Christ within us. The Visitation teaches us what to do after Communion: go in haste to serve, and bring joy.
outline: Ask: what is the first thing you do after receiving good news?
Mary “went with haste” to serve. Receiving Christ leads to mission.
John recognises Christ before birth: a word on the dignity of the unborn.
God lifts the lowly and fills the hungry. Mary's song is a programme of Christian life.
The 25-day Nombu begins: prayer, fasting and visiting someone who needs us.
“Blessed is she who believed.” Blessed are we when we believe.
live: Visit someone (Luke 1:39)
During the Nombu, visit an elderly, sick or lonely person in your family or parish.
Pray the Magnificat (Luke 1:46–55)
Pray Mary's song each evening this week, slowly, thanking God for one gift of the day.
Keep the 25-day Nombu
Decide now how your family will keep the fast from 1 December: food, screens, and charity.
fathers: St Ambrose of Milan
“Let the soul of Mary be in each one of you to magnify the Lord; let the spirit of Mary be in each one to rejoice in God” (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 2, 26).
St Bede the Venerable
He calls the Magnificat a song to be sung daily by the Church, because it teaches us to give glory to God for the gift of the Incarnation (Homilies on the Gospels I, 4).
magis: Redemptoris Mater 12
In the Visitation Mary is blessed for her faith; Elizabeth's words reveal the “obedience of faith” by which Mary welcomed the Word.
Evangelii Gaudium 288
Mary is the woman who “sets out in haste”; there is a Marian “style” in the Church's evangelising work: tenderness, humility and service.
Catechism 2676
The words of Elizabeth, together with the angel's greeting, form the first part of the Hail Mary.
saints: 30 Nov: St Andrew, Apostle. 1 Dec: beginning of the Twenty-Five Days Nombu. 3 Dec: St Francis Xavier. 4 Dec: St John Damascene. Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-11-29.prayer: Lord God, Mary carried your Son in haste to Elizabeth and filled her house with joy. As we begin the fast before Yaldo, make us carry Christ to those who need him, and let our souls, with hers, magnify your name. Amen.

2026-11-02.title: Monday after Qudos Eetho Sunday
2026-11-02.verse: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
theo: On the day after the Church was sanctified in the liturgy, St Paul tells the Thessalonians plainly what God wants: their holiness. “For God did not call us to impurity but in holiness.” Holiness is not a feeling; it is a way of living in the body, in marriage, in business, in every relationship, so that no brother is wronged.

On the mountain Jesus paints the portrait of the holy person: poor in spirit, mourning, meek, hungry for justice, merciful, pure in heart, a peacemaker, persecuted for his sake. It is first of all his own portrait. To live the Beatitudes is to let his face appear in ours, and the promise is the greatest of all: the pure in heart will see God.
outline: Ask: what does God want from me today?
Holiness is God's will for everyone.
The kingdom belongs to the humble.
“Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.”
live: Pray the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3–10)
Choose one Beatitude and live it today.
Guard your heart (1 Thessalonians 4:4)
Avoid one occasion of sin you know well.
2026-11-02.prayer: Holy Father, you have called us not to impurity but to holiness. Give us a pure heart, that we may see you, and make us poor in spirit, meek and merciful like your Son. Amen.

2026-11-03.title: Tuesday after Qudos Eetho Sunday · The 318 Fathers of Nicaea
2026-11-03.alt: Alternative Gospels: John 10:11–18, John 14:1–6 or John 15:9–17. Memorial of Paulose Mar Philoxenos (1998). The 318 Fathers of the Council of Nicaea.
2026-11-03.verse: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
theo: Hebrews asks us to remember our leaders, those who spoke the word of God to us, and to imitate their faith. Today the Church remembers the bishops of the Council of Nicaea (AD 325), whom tradition numbers as 318. They confessed the Son “one in being with the Father”, the faith we still sing in the Creed. Their teaching stands because Christ himself does not change: “the same yesterday and today and forever.”

In the Gospel Jesus praises the faithful and wise servant whom the master puts in charge of his household “to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time.” That is the work of every shepherd in the Church, and of every parent at home: to feed others faithfully, not to lord it over them, because the master may come at any hour.
outline: Who handed the faith on to you?
Imitate the faith of those who taught us.
The Creed of Nicaea is our faith today.
Feed others at the proper time.
“Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
live: Pray the Creed (Hebrews 13:8)
Say the Nicene Creed slowly today.
Pray for your shepherds (Hebrews 13:7)
Pray for your bishop and for the bishops who have died.
2026-11-03.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, the same yesterday, today and forever, we thank you for the Fathers of Nicaea and for all who handed on the faith to us. Make us faithful and wise servants, ready for your coming. Amen.

2026-11-04.title: Wednesday after Qudos Eetho Sunday
readings: What do you have that you did not receive?
2026-11-04.verse: Do not judge, and you will not be judged; do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven;
theo: The Corinthians were proud of their favourite preachers and of their own gifts. Paul brings them down to earth with one question: “What do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as if it were not a gift?” Our talents, our faith, even our good works are gifts. The apostles, by contrast, live as “fools for the sake of Christ”, hungry and homeless, blessing when reviled.

Jesus draws the conclusion for daily life: do not judge, do not condemn, forgive, give. The measure we use for others will be used for us. And he adds the famous picture of the speck and the log: we see the small fault in our brother's eye and do not notice the beam in our own. Humility before God makes us gentle with others.
outline: Ask: how often today did I judge someone?
What do you have that you did not receive?
Point 3 · The log in my eye
live: Thank God for a gift (1 Corinthians 4:7)
Name three gifts you received and did not earn.
Hold back a judgment (Luke 6:37)
When you are about to criticise someone today, pray for them instead.
2026-11-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, everything I have is your gift. Take away my pride, keep me from judging others, and help me to see first the log in my own eye. Amen.

2026-11-05.title: Thursday after Qudos Eetho Sunday
readings: The Lord disciplines those he loves
The Son does what he sees the Father doing
2026-11-05.verse: Now, discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
theo: Hebrews speaks to Christians tired of struggling. Their trials are not a sign that God has abandoned them but that he treats them as sons and daughters: “the Lord disciplines those whom he loves.” Every good parent corrects a child; God trains us “for our good, in order that we may share his holiness.” What hurts now bears fruit later: the peaceful fruit of righteousness.

In the Gospel Jesus reveals his own sonship. The Son does nothing on his own, “but only what he sees the Father doing.” The Father loves the Son and shows him everything; he gives him power to give life and to judge, “so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.” Our sonship is a share in his: like him, we learn to watch the Father and do what he does.
outline: Remember a correction that later helped you.
God trains us as his children.
Jesus does what he sees the Father doing.
To honour Jesus is to honour the Father.
“Later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness.”
live: Accept one correction (Hebrews 12:5)
Receive a correction today without excuses.
Watch the Father (John 5:19)
Before deciding something today, ask: what would the Father do?
2026-11-05.prayer: Father, you train us as your children. Help us to accept your discipline with trust, to watch what you do as your Son did, and to honour him in all things. Amen.

2026-11-06.title: Friday after Qudos Eetho Sunday
2026-11-06.verse: Therefore, I tell you, her sins, which were many, have been forgiven; hence she has shown great love.
theo: Paul tells Timothy what to say to the rich: not to be haughty, not to hope in uncertain riches but in God, who richly provides everything for our enjoyment; to be rich in good works, generous and ready to share. Money is a good servant and a cruel master. Shared, it becomes “a good foundation for the future”.

At Simon's table a woman known as a sinner bathes Jesus' feet with her tears, dries them with her hair and anoints them. Simon sees only her past; Jesus sees her love. The one who is forgiven much loves much. On Friday, the day of the Cross, we stand with her at his feet: “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
outline: Ask: what am I rich in?
Hope in God, not in money.
“Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
live: Share something (1 Timothy 6:18)
Give something today to a person in need.
Weep for your sins (Luke 7:38)
Spend five minutes before a crucifix in sorrow and thanks.
2026-11-06.prayer: Merciful Lord, you received the tears of the sinful woman and forgave her much. Free me from trust in riches, make me rich in good works, and let my love grow from your forgiveness. Amen.

2026-11-07.title: Saturday after Qudos Eetho Sunday · The 33 Martyrs of Melitene
readings: Sir, we wish to see Jesus
2026-11-07.alt: Commemoration of the thirty-three martyrs of Melitene (in present-day Turkey), soldiers remembered in the Eastern calendars; little is known of them for certain (Tradition).
2026-11-07.verse: They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and said to him, “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.”
theo: The Church in Corinth was splitting into parties: “I belong to Paul,” “I belong to Apollos,” “I belong to Cephas,” “I belong to Christ.” Paul's answer is sharp: “Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you?” Every preacher is only a servant. Paul was sent “to proclaim the gospel, and not with eloquent wisdom, so that the cross of Christ might not be emptied of its power.”

In the Gospel some Greeks come to Philip with a request that every parish should hear: “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.” People do not come to church to see us, our quarrels or our cleverness, but to see him. A united community that points away from itself to Christ is the best answer to that request. The martyrs we remember today gave the same answer with their lives.
outline: What do people see when they look at our parish?
Divisions empty the Cross of its power.
The word of God does its own work.
Point 3 · We wish to see Jesus
Point people to him, not to us.
live: Heal a division (1 Corinthians 1:10)
Speak kindly today to someone from whom you are estranged.
Show Jesus (John 12:21)
Bring one person closer to Christ this week by an invitation or a kindness.
2026-11-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are not divided. Heal the divisions in our families and parishes, keep us faithful like the martyrs, and let all who wish to see you find you in us. Amen.

2026-11-09.title: Monday after Hudos Eetho Sunday · St Theodore
readings: A sabbath rest remains for the people of God
Not one of these little ones should be lost
2026-11-09.alt: St Theodore, soldier and martyr (early 4th century; details of his life come mainly from Tradition).
2026-11-09.verse: So it is not the will of your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost.
theo: Hebrews reads Psalm 95 as a call for today: “O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts.” Israel in the desert did not enter God's rest because of disobedience. But the promise still stands: “a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God.” Every Sunday Qurbono is a foretaste of that rest, and every day is the “today” in which we can listen.

In the Gospel Jesus defends the little ones: children, the weak, the easily forgotten. Their angels always behold the Father's face. The shepherd leaves the ninety-nine to look for the one that strayed, and rejoices more over it than over the rest. The Father does not want even one of them to be lost. A parish is judged by how it seeks the one who is missing.
outline: Who is missing from our parish today?
Point 2 · Their angels see the Father
Point 3 · The shepherd seeks the lost
God's joy over one who returns.
“Not one of these little ones should be lost.”
live: Listen today (Hebrews 4:7)
Read the day's Gospel before you check your phone.
Seek one (Matthew 18:12)
Call or visit someone who no longer comes to church.
2026-11-09.prayer: Good Shepherd, you seek the one who is lost. Soften our hearts to hear your voice today, keep us from despising the little ones, and bring us all into your rest. Amen.

2026-11-10.title: Tuesday after Hudos Eetho Sunday · The Prophet Samuel; St Leo the Great
2026-11-10.alt: The Prophet Samuel. St Leo the Great, Pope (died 461), Doctor of the Church.
2026-11-10.verse: So the last will be first, and the first will be last.
theo: Paul's words to Christian slaves sound strange to us, but their core is clear: whatever our station, we serve so that “the name of God and the teaching may not be blasphemed”, and we serve a believing master “all the more” because he is a brother. Work done well and honestly is a witness to Christ in every office, field and kitchen.

In the parable the owner goes out at dawn, at nine, at noon, at three and at five to call workers into his vineyard, and pays the last the same as the first. Those who worked all day grumble. “Are you envious because I am generous?” God's call comes at every hour, and his reward is not wages but himself. Samuel heard the call as a boy; Leo the Great served as Pope in hard times. Each answered when called.
outline: When did God first call you?
It is never too late to answer.
Do not envy his goodness to others.
Point 3 · Speak, your servant is listening
“Are you envious because I am generous?”
live: Work as service (1 Timothy 6:2)
Do your work today as an offering to God.
Rejoice in another's grace (Matthew 20:15)
Thank God for a blessing given to someone else.
2026-11-10.prayer: Lord of the vineyard, you call us at every hour and pay beyond our deserving. Free us from envy, make our work an offering, and give us Samuel's listening heart. Amen.

2026-11-11.title: Wednesday after Hudos Eetho Sunday
2026-11-11.verse: For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.
theo: The temple in Jerusalem had a wall that kept Gentiles out of the inner courts. Paul says that on the Cross Christ has broken down every such wall: Jews and Gentiles are reconciled “in one body”, no longer strangers and aliens but “members of the household of God”, built on the apostles and prophets with Christ as cornerstone. The Church is a living temple, still under construction, where God dwells in the Spirit.

In the Gospel John's disciples ask why Jesus' disciples do not fast. While the bridegroom is with them they cannot mourn; the days will come when he is taken away, and then they will fast. Jesus brings something new that cannot be squeezed into old forms: new wine needs fresh wineskins. At the start of a new liturgical year we ask him to renew the wineskins of our hearts.
outline: What walls divide our families and parishes?
The Cross breaks down the wall.
Built together on Christ the cornerstone.
live: Cross a wall (Ephesians 2:14)
Greet someone you usually avoid.
Fast with purpose (Matthew 9:15)
Choose a small fast this week as a sign of longing for the Bridegroom.
2026-11-11.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are our peace and the cornerstone of your Church. Break down the walls between us, build us into your temple, and pour your new wine into renewed hearts. Amen.

2026-11-12.title: Thursday after Hudos Eetho Sunday · St John the Almsgiver
readings: The eyes of your heart enlightened
2026-11-12.alt: Mar Yohannan of Alexandria, St John the Almsgiver, Patriarch of Alexandria (early 7th century), remembered for his care of the poor (History; many stories of his charity are Tradition).
2026-11-12.verse: The kingdom of God is as if someone would scatter seed on the ground, and would sleep and rise night and day, and the seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.
theo: Paul prays that the Ephesians may have “the eyes of your heart enlightened” to know the hope of their calling, the riches of their inheritance and the immeasurable power of God, the same power that raised Christ from the dead and seated him above every power. Christ is head over all things “for the church, which is his body.” Faith is not only knowing about God; it is seeing with the heart.

In Mark's short parable a farmer sows, sleeps and rises, and the seed grows “he does not know how”: first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain. God's kingdom grows quietly, by God's power, often unseen. St John the Almsgiver, Patriarch of Alexandria, sowed generously among the poor and trusted God with the harvest.
outline: Have you seen something grow while you slept?
Point 1 · The seed grows by itself
“The seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.”
live: Trust the growth (Mark 4:27)
Hand over to God one worry about a child or a project.
Give alms (Proverbs 19:17)
Give something to the poor today in secret.
2026-11-12.prayer: Lord of the harvest, the seed of your word grows by your power. Enlighten the eyes of our hearts, make us patient sowers, and generous like St John the Almsgiver. Amen.

2026-11-13.title: Friday after Hudos Eetho Sunday · St John Chrysostom
readings: God's wisdom revealed through the Spirit
The treasure, the pearl and the net
2026-11-13.alt: Mar Ivanios (John) Chrysostom, “golden-mouthed”, Archbishop of Constantinople, died in exile in 407; Doctor of the Church. Name day of Youhanon Mar Chrysostom.
2026-11-13.verse: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls; on finding one pearl of great value, he went and sold all that he had and bought it.
theo: Paul speaks of a wisdom “not of this age”, hidden and now revealed: if the rulers of this age had understood it, “they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” What no eye has seen God has prepared for those who love him, and “these things God has revealed to us through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.” The gospel is not a clever theory but a gift received in the Spirit.

Jesus speaks of a man who finds treasure in a field and “in his joy” sells everything to buy it, and of a merchant who sells all for one pearl. The kingdom is worth everything. St John Chrysostom, the great preacher of Antioch and Constantinople, gave his golden words and finally his freedom for that pearl; he died in exile, and his Liturgy is still prayed across the East.
outline: What would you sell everything for?
Point 2 · Wisdom revealed by the Spirit
Not the wisdom of this age.
“In his joy he goes and sells all that he has.”
live: Choose the pearl (Matthew 13:46)
Give up one thing today that keeps you from God.
Read a Father (1 Corinthians 2:13)
Read a page of St John Chrysostom or another Church Father.
2026-11-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the treasure hidden in the field and the pearl of great value. Give us joy to choose you above all, and through the prayers of St John Chrysostom, wisdom that comes from your Spirit. Amen.

2026-11-14.title: Saturday after Hudos Eetho Sunday · Mar Philipose Shleeha (St Philip the Apostle)
readings: Whoever has seen me has seen the Father
2026-11-14.alt: St Philip the Apostle, from Bethsaida in Galilee.
2026-11-14.verse: Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you all this time, Philip, and you still do not know me? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.
theo: Paul asks to be regarded “as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries”, and the one thing required of stewards is that they be found trustworthy. He does not even judge himself; the Lord will judge, and he “will bring to light the things now hidden in darkness and will disclose the purposes of the heart.” Every priest, catechist and parent is such a steward: not owner, but servant.

Philip, the apostle we honour today, makes an honest request at the Last Supper: “Lord, show us the Father, and we will be satisfied.” Jesus answers with one of the most astonishing sentences of the Gospel: “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.” In the face of Jesus we see God. And he promises that whatever we ask in his name, he will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
outline: Point 2 · Leave judgment to the Lord
He sees the purposes of the heart.
“Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.”
live: Be trustworthy (1 Corinthians 4:2)
Keep one promise today exactly.
Look at Jesus (John 14:9)
Spend five minutes before an icon of Christ.
2026-11-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, in you we see the Father. Make us faithful stewards of your mysteries, and through the prayers of St Philip, satisfy our hearts with the sight of your face. Amen.

2026-11-16.title: Monday after the Sunday of the Message to Zechariah · Mar Mathai Shleeha (St Matthew the Apostle)
readings: Lead a life worthy of your calling
2026-11-16.verse: Go and learn what this means, ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.
theo: Matthew sat at the tax booth, a collaborator with Rome, despised by his people. Jesus looked at him and said two words: “Follow me.” And he got up and followed him. That evening Jesus ate at Matthew's house with tax collectors and sinners, and when the Pharisees objected he quoted Hosea: “I desire mercy, not sacrifice.” The doctor goes to the sick. Matthew, once a counter of coins, became the writer of the first Gospel.

Paul, a prisoner for the Lord, begs the Ephesians to live a life worthy of their calling, “with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love”, keeping the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace: one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. Every call, like Matthew's, is a call into one family.
outline: What were you doing when God called you?
The doctor comes for the sick.
“I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”
live: Get up and follow (Matthew 9:9)
Do at once one good thing you have been postponing.
Bear with one another (Ephesians 4:2)
Be patient today with one person who tests you.
2026-11-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, you called Matthew from his tax booth and ate with sinners. Call us again today, heal us with your mercy, and help us live worthy of our calling in humility and love. Amen.

2026-11-17.title: Tuesday after the Sunday of the Message to Zechariah
2026-11-17.verse: And just then some people were carrying a paralyzed man lying on a bed. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
theo: Paul compares God's people to an olive tree. Some natural branches were broken off; the Gentiles, a wild olive shoot, were grafted in to share “the rich root”. So he warns: “do not boast over the branches… it is not you that support the root, but the root that supports you.” We stand by faith and by grace alone, and God can graft back in those who were cut off. Humility, not pride, is the right response to being included.

Friends carry a paralysed man to Jesus. Seeing their faith, Jesus first says what no one expected: “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.” The scribes call it blasphemy. So Jesus heals the man's body too, “so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.” The crowds glorify God “who had given such authority to human beings”: the authority that Christ still exercises through his Church in Confession.
outline: “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
live: Carry someone (Matthew 9:2)
Pray by name for someone who cannot pray for themselves.
Go to Confession (Matthew 9:6)
Plan a confession before the Christmas fast begins on 1 December.
2026-11-17.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of friends and forgave the paralysed man. Forgive our sins, heal our weakness, and keep us humble branches on your living tree. Amen.

2026-11-18.title: Wednesday after the Sunday of the Message to Zechariah
readings: The Lord be with your spirit
As a hen gathers her brood
2026-11-18.verse: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
theo: The last lines of Paul's last letter are a list of names: Prisca and Aquila, the household of Onesiphorus, Erastus, Trophimus left ill at Miletus, Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia. The great apostle, near death, remembers people. Then a blessing that echoes in every Syriac liturgy: “The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you.” The Church is a web of friendships held together by grace.

Jesus looks at Jerusalem and weeps with a mother's heart: “How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!” God's love is tender and persistent, but it never forces. The door stays open until the day they will say, “Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord”, the cry we sing at every Holy Qurbono.
outline: Whose names are in your prayers?
God's love is a mother's love.
Point 3 · Blessed is he who comes
The Church's cry at every Qurbono.
“As a hen gathers her brood under her wings.”
live: Pray by name (2 Timothy 4:19)
Write the names of ten people and pray for each today.
Come under his wings (Matthew 23:37)
Bring one fear to Jesus in prayer and leave it there.
2026-11-18.prayer: Lord Jesus, you long to gather us as a hen gathers her brood. Make us willing to come under your wings, and keep in your grace all whose names we carry in our hearts. Amen.

2026-11-19.title: Thursday after the Sunday of the Message to Zechariah
readings: Children and parents in the Lord
The greatest among you will be your servant
2026-11-19.verse: The greatest among you will be your servant.
theo: Paul turns to the Christian home. Children are to obey their parents “in the Lord” and honour father and mother, the first commandment with a promise. And fathers are told something revolutionary for their time: “do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.” Authority in a Christian family is a service of love, not a tool of control.

Jesus criticises leaders who “do not practice what they teach”, who tie heavy burdens on others and love the best seats and titles. Among his disciples it must be different: one teacher, one Father, one instructor, the Messiah. “The greatest among you will be your servant.” Whether at home or in the Church, the one who serves most is greatest in God's sight.
outline: Point 2 · Parents who do not provoke
“The greatest among you will be your servant.”
live: Honour your parents (Ephesians 6:2)
Call or visit your parents, or pray for them if they have died.
Serve at home (Matthew 23:11)
Do one household task without being asked.
2026-11-19.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came to serve. Bless our homes: make children obedient and loving, parents patient and gentle, and all of us servants of one another in your name. Amen.

2026-11-20.title: Friday after the Sunday of the Message to Zechariah
2026-11-20.verse: For, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
theo: Salvation is not far away, Paul says, as if we had to climb to heaven or descend to the abyss to fetch Christ. “The word is near you, on your lips and in your heart.” If you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. There is no distinction between Jew and Greek: the same Lord is generous to all who call on him.

Jesus tells of a sower who throws seed everywhere: on the path, on rocky ground, among thorns, and on good soil. The sower is not stingy; the seed is the same; the difference is the soil. Some hearts are hard as a path, some shallow, some choked with worries. But the good soil yields thirty, sixty, a hundredfold. Each day we choose what kind of soil we will be.
outline: What kind of soil am I today?
On your lips and in your heart.
“Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
live: Confess with your lips (Romans 10:9)
Say “Jesus is Lord” aloud in your morning prayer.
Clear a thorn (Matthew 13:7)
Remove one distraction that chokes your prayer.
2026-11-20.prayer: Lord Jesus, your word is near us. Make our hearts good soil, clear away the thorns of worry, and let us call on your name and be saved. Amen.

2026-11-21.title: The Entry of Mary, Mother of God, into the Temple
readings: Whoever does the will of my Father
2026-11-21.alt: Feast of the Presentation (Entry) of the Mother of God in the Temple. The story of the child Mary brought to the Temple by Joachim and Anne comes from early Christian Tradition (the Protoevangelium of James), not from Scripture; the feast celebrates her total dedication to God.
2026-11-21.verse: For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
theo: The Church celebrates today the tradition that Mary, as a little child, was brought by her parents Joachim and Anne to the Temple and given to God. The details come from Tradition, not from the Gospels, but the meaning is biblical: like Samuel, whom Hannah “lent to the LORD”, Mary belonged wholly to God from the beginning. The little girl in the Temple would one day become the Temple, carrying God's Son in her womb.

In the Gospel Jesus' mother and brothers stand outside wanting to speak with him. Pointing to his disciples he says: “Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.” This is not a rejection of Mary but her highest praise: no one did the Father's will more completely than she who said, “let it be with me according to your word.” Paul's words fit her perfectly: rejoice, do not worry, pray with thanksgiving, think on whatever is true, honourable, just, pure and lovely.
outline: What did your parents give to God when they baptised you?
Mary, like Samuel, belongs to the Lord.
The peace of God guards our hearts.
“Whoever does the will of my Father is my mother.”
live: Offer the children (1 Samuel 1:28)
Parents: consecrate your children to God through Mary today.
Think on what is lovely (Philippians 4:8)
Replace one negative conversation with a good word.
2026-11-21.prayer: Holy Mary, Mother of God, given to the Lord from childhood, teach us to belong wholly to God, to do the Father's will, and to rejoice always in your Son. Amen.

2026-11-23.title: Monday after the Sunday of the Annunciation · St Clement, Pope; St Felicity
readings: The hearts of the saints refreshed
A tree is known by its fruit
2026-11-23.alt: St Clement of Rome, Pope (late 1st century), author of a letter to the Church in Corinth (History); St Felicity, Roman martyr (Tradition). Anniversary of the erection of the Eparchy of St Ephrem of Khadki (2019).
2026-11-23.verse: The good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good, and the evil person out of evil treasure produces evil; for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks.
theo: The short letter to Philemon begins with warmth. Paul, a prisoner, thanks God for Philemon's love and faith, and tells him: “the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, my brother.” Some Christians are like a cool drink on a hot day; their love refreshes everyone around them. Their goodness flows from a heart rooted in Christ.

Jesus says the same in a picture: a good tree does not bear bad fruit; each tree is known by its own fruit. Figs do not grow on thorns. And the fruit of the human tree is above all our words: “it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks.” To change our speech we must change our heart; to change our heart we must stay close to the one who is good. St Clement, who wrote to the quarrelling Corinthians, knew that peace in the Church begins in the heart.
outline: What do my words reveal about my heart?
“Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.”
live: Watch your words (Luke 6:45)
Speak no word of complaint today.
Refresh someone (Philemon 7)
Encourage a tired person with a visit, call or message.
2026-11-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, make my heart a good treasure, so that my words may bring life. Through the prayers of St Clement and St Felicity, let my love refresh the hearts of your saints. Amen.

2026-11-24.title: Tuesday after the Sunday of the Annunciation
readings: The grace of God has appeared
2026-11-24.alt: The Christmas fast (Twenty-Five Days' Fast) begins on Tuesday 1 December.
2026-11-24.verse: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all,
theo: Titus 2 is read at Christmas in many Churches: “the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all.” In the child of Bethlehem God's kindness took a human face. That grace is also a teacher: it trains us to renounce impiety and worldly passions and to live self-controlled, upright and godly lives, while we wait for “the blessed hope and the manifestation of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.” We live between two comings.

Jesus tells his disciples to learn from the fig tree: when its branches become tender and put forth leaves, summer is near. So too the signs of his coming. “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.” No one knows the day or hour; therefore we live each day attentively. A week before the Christmas fast begins, we are invited to read the signs and prepare our hearts.
outline: What signs tell you Christmas is coming?
God's kindness has a human face.
Point 3 · My words will not pass away
“The grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all.”
live: Prepare for the fast (Titus 2:12)
Decide today how you will keep the Twenty-Five Days' Fast from 1 December.
Trust his word (Matthew 24:35)
Learn one verse of Scripture by heart this week.
2026-11-24.prayer: Lord Jesus, in you the grace of God has appeared. Train us to live soberly and justly, keep us watchful for your coming, and let your word, which never passes away, be our light. Amen.

2026-11-25.title: Wednesday after the Sunday of the Annunciation
readings: Christ is proclaimed, and in that I rejoice
Blessed are your eyes, for they see
2026-11-25.verse: But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.
theo: Paul is in chains, and some preachers are using his imprisonment to make themselves look better. His reaction is astonishing: “What does it matter? Just this, that Christ is proclaimed in every way, whether out of false motives or true; and in that I rejoice.” He is free of rivalry because his only concern is that Christ be exalted in his body, “whether by life or by death.”

The disciples ask why Jesus speaks in parables. Parables are an invitation: those who want to understand lean in and ask; those who do not, hear without hearing. Isaiah foresaw a people whose hearts had grown dull. “But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear. Truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see.” We are among those who now see; what we do with that gift is our responsibility.

2026-11-26.verse: They were all amazed and kept saying to one another, “What kind of utterance is this? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and out they come!”
theo: Paul warns the Corinthians to flee from idolatry, and gives a reason that is pure Eucharistic theology: “The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?” Those who share the Lord's table cannot also share the table of demons. The Holy Qurbono binds us to Christ and to one another; it excludes every other lord.

In the synagogue at Capernaum the people are astounded at Jesus' teaching, “because he spoke with authority.” A man with an unclean spirit cries out: “I know who you are, the Holy One of God.” Jesus rebukes the spirit and it leaves him. His word is not just information; it is power that frees. The same word is spoken over the bread and cup at our altar.

2026-11-27.verse: Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.
theo: Some Thessalonians, expecting the Lord's return at any moment, had stopped working and were living as busybodies. Paul reminds them that he and his companions worked “night and day” so as not to burden anyone, and gives a blunt rule: anyone unwilling to work should not eat. Then a word for all who are tired of doing good: “Brothers and sisters, do not be weary in doing what is right.” Faith makes us responsible, not idle.

When the Pharisees ask about divorce, Jesus takes them back beyond Moses' concession, which was given “because of your hardness of heart”, to the beginning of creation: God made them male and female, and the two become one flesh. “Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.” Christian marriage is a covenant God himself seals; in the Syriac tradition the crowning of bride and groom shows that their union is holy and royal.

theo: Paul writes as a father, not a schoolmaster: “though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.” He sends Timothy to remind them of his ways, and warns those who are puffed up: “the kingdom of God depends not on talk but on power.” Spiritual fatherhood and motherhood are a great gift in the Church: parents, godparents, priests and catechists who give birth to faith in others.

The kingdom, Jesus says, is like a mustard seed, the smallest of seeds, which becomes a great shrub where birds nest in its shade. Ezekiel had seen God plant a tender shoot that became a noble cedar. The Church began with twelve men and a few women; in India it began with one apostle on the coast of Kerala. On the last Saturday before the new liturgical season of fasting, we trust that small beginnings in God's hands bear great fruit.

One of them is Andrew, and the first thing he does is find his brother Simon: “We have found the Messiah.” He brings him to Jesus. qa: What does Qudos Eetho mean?
The Sanctification of the Church. On this Sunday the Syro-Malankara liturgical year begins by remembering that God has made the Church holy and chosen her as his dwelling.
Why does our liturgical year begin with the Church?
Because it is in the Church that we celebrate all the mysteries of Christ through the year. The Church is the place where God dwells among his people (CCC 1066–1068).
What did Jesus mean when he called Peter the rock?
Jesus made Peter the visible foundation of the Church's unity and gave him the keys of the Kingdom. The Pope, as Peter's successor, continues this ministry (CCC 881–882).
What happened in 1930?

On 20 September 1930 Archbishop Mar Ivanios and his companions entered full communion with the Catholic Church while keeping their West Syriac liturgy. This was the beginning of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today a new liturgical year begins, and our Church begins it in a very wise way: not with Christmas, but with the Church herself. Qudos Eetho, the Sanctification of the Church. Before we celebrate the mysteries of Christ, we remember the house in which we celebrate them.

Listen to the long story told in our readings. Moses sets up the Tabernacle; Solomon builds the Temple; Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord leave the Temple because the people had defiled it; Isaiah sees the Lord on his throne and hears the seraphim cry, “Holy, holy, holy.” God wants to live among his people, but his holiness can never be taken for granted.

Then St Peter tells us where God lives now: in us. “Like living stones, let yourselves be built into a spiritual house.” Every baptised person is a stone in God's house. Some stones carry weight; some stones crumble. This year, what kind of stone will I be?

And in the Gospel Jesus says to Peter: “On this rock I will build my church.” For us Syro-Malankara Catholics these words are dear. In 1930 Mar Ivanios led our forefathers into communion with the successor of Peter, while keeping our ancient Syriac liturgy. Unity with Peter and love for our own tradition are not two loyalties; they are one Catholic faith.
In a few moments we will sing with the seraphim, “Holy, holy, holy.” Heaven's song in our parish church. Let us begin this year as living stones, holy, united and faithful. Amen.
kids: Children, what is a church built with? Stones and bricks! But God's Church is built with people. You are a living stone in God's house!
And the most important stone is Jesus. He holds everything together. Peter said, “You are the Christ,” and Jesus built his Church on Peter's faith.
This year, be a strong stone: come to Holy Qurbono, help in the parish, and be kind. Let's say together: “I am a living stone for Jesus!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a new liturgical year begins today with Qudos Eetho, the Sanctification of the Church. Among the readings is the vision of the prophet Isaiah in the Temple (Isaiah 6:1–8). It is worth looking at closely, because we repeat its words in every Holy Qurbono.

In the year that King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up. Seraphim stood above Him and called to one another: holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory (Isaiah 6:1–3). The king had died; the nation was anxious. But Isaiah saw the true King, who never dies. When we sing Qadeesh in the Qurbono, we join the seraphim, and with them we see the King.

Isaiah's first reaction was not joy but fear: woe is me, for I am a man of unclean lips. Then a seraph took a burning coal from the altar and touched his lips, saying: your guilt has departed and your sin is blotted out (Isaiah 6:5–7). The Fathers of the Syriac Church saw in this burning coal an image of the Holy Mysteries, the Body of Christ received from the altar, which purifies and sets on fire. Before we receive, let us confess, as Isaiah did, that we are unworthy.

Then the Lord asked: whom shall I send? And Isaiah answered: here am I; send me (Isaiah 6:8). A holy God sends a holy people. In the Gospel Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God, and Jesus builds His Church on that faith (Matthew 16:16–18). The Church is not a club for the holy; she is a people being made holy and sent into the world.

So as this new year begins, let us do three things. Let us sing the Qadeesh with attention, knowing that heaven sings with us. Let us prepare well for Holy Communion, with a clean conscience. And let us say to God: here am I, send me. Offer yourself for one service in your parish this year.
